The wedge is worked from the top edge after row 17: sc 12, turn, sc 12, turn, sc 6, turn, sc 6, turn.
caption: Four extra rows at the top, two in the middle, none at the bottom. That is a taper of 0.8 inch.

alt: A foundation chain of 19. The chain nearest the hook is skipped and the first sc goes into the 2nd chain from the hook, so row 1 has 18 sc.
caption: Step 1. The chain is the height of the sleeve, 18 sc for a 4.5 inch cup. Rows run around the cup.

alt: The sleeve strip drawn with each row as a column 18 stitches tall and the top edge at the top. Between rows 17 and 18 sit four short rows worked from the top edge: two of 12 stitches and two of 6. The top edge gains four rows and the bottom edge none, which is what makes the top 39 rows long and the bottom 35.
caption: Step 2. The short rows add length only to the top edge, which is what lets a straight strip follow a wider rim.

alt: A sage crochet drawstring bag around a plain wine bottle
caption: Illustration. A tube and a drawstring. Not a tested fit on a real bottle.

alt: Sage cotton yarn, a hook, and a plain bottle
caption: Illustration. Yarn and a hook. Not a weighed amount.

alt: A bottle in a straight tube. The flat base of 40 stitches sits under the bottle and adds no height. The sides rise from round 8 for 9 inches, 45 rounds, to just above the shoulder, where the eyelet round and two more rounds gather around the neck. An optional handle is sewn to solid rounds below the eyelets.
caption: Count side rounds from the end of the base. The base lies under the bottle.

alt: Four steps. 1: wrap the yarn around two fingers so the tail crosses over the working yarn. 2: insert the hook under the ring, catch the working yarn, and pull up a loop, then ch 1; the ch 1 is not a stitch. 3: work the stated number of sc into the ring, over both strands of the ring and the tail. 4: pull the tail to close the center, then count the stitches.
caption: The base starts in a magic ring, closed tight so the bottle cannot push through.

alt: Base: rounds 1 to 7, drawn as rings from the center out. Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring, 6 stitches. Round 2: 2 sc in each st, 12 stitches. Round 3: (2 sc in next, sc in next) 6 times, 18 stitches. Round 4: (2 sc in next, sc 2) 6 times, 24 stitches. Round 5: (2 sc in next, sc 3) 6 times, 30 stitches. Round 6: (2 sc in next, sc 4) 6 times, 36 stitches. Round 7: (2 sc in next, sc 8) 4 times, 40 stitches.
caption: Step 1. Rounds 2 to 6 add 6 each. Round 7 adds 4 to land on 40, an even count for the eyelets.

alt: Eyelet round on 40, drawn as rings from the center out. Round 52: undefined, 40 stitches. Eyelet round: (sc in next, ch 1, skip 1) 20 times: 20 sc, 20 stitches.
caption: Step 2. The eyelet round keeps the stitch positions: 20 sc and 20 chain spaces, back to 40 sc on the next round.

alt: The whole bag by stitch count, as bars sized by stitch count. Round 1: 6, Round 2: 12, Round 3: 18, Round 4: 24, Round 5: 30, Round 6: 36, Round 7: 40, Rounds 8 to 52: 40, Round 53: 20+20, Round 54: 40, Round 55: 40. R53 to R55 are the pattern's eyelet round (20 sc and 20 chain spaces), next round, and last round.
caption: Step 3. The whole bag by stitch count. The 7 base rounds lie flat and add no height.

alt: An oatmeal crochet ear warmer headband
caption: Illustration. A wide ribbed loop. Not a fitted sample.

alt: Worsted yarn, a hook, and a tape measure
caption: Illustration. Yardage is not a weighed band.

alt: Back-loop single crochet in oatmeal yarn
caption: Illustration. The rib is the back loop. The strip is still flat.

alt: The flat band beside a tape measure
caption: Illustration. Measure the relaxed strip. Do not stretch it to the example.

alt: The short ends sewn into a loop
caption: Illustration. Sew the short ends. Do not twist the band.

alt: The ear warmer next to a beanie
caption: Illustration. The beanie is a separate project, not part of this band.

alt: Diagram of a short ribbed strip. The starting chain is the width. The rows run out to the side and become the circumference. More chains widen the band. More rows lengthen the loop.
caption: Width and circumference are different edges. Do not add rows to fix a narrow band.

alt: A foundation chain of 13. The chain nearest the hook is skipped and the first sc goes into the 2nd chain from the hook, so row 1 has 12 sc.
caption: Chain 13 for 12 sc. The chain is the band's width, about 3.4 inches at 3.5 per inch.

alt: Two steps. 1: the top of each stitch has a front loop, nearer you, and a back loop, farther away. For the rib, insert the hook under the back loop only. 2: the front loops left behind form a raised ridge on every row. The fabric stretches across the ridges, in the direction the rows stack up, so a band worked sideways stretches around the head.
caption: Every row from row 2 goes into the back loop only. The unworked front loops become the ribs.

alt: Diagram of two short ends sewn in line, beside a join where one end is flipped so the rib spirals.
caption: Match the ends, then sew. A twist is a flipped end, not a short row count.

alt: A sage crochet pouch with a wood button and a white earbud case
caption: Illustration. A sage pouch with a button flap. Not a pouch fitted to a measured case.

alt: Sage yarn, a hook, a wood button, and a white charging case
caption: Illustration. The case is the size guide. Not a weighed amount of yarn.

alt: The buttoned flap with the case inside
caption: Illustration. The loop is chain stitches. The button is sewn, not crocheted.

alt: A case footprint of 1.9 by 0.9 inches with a perimeter of 5.6 inches, shown inside a round pouch tube. A table at 4 single crochet per inch: 24 stitches is 6.0 inches around and snug, 27 is 6.75 inches and the example choice, 30 is 7.5 inches and roomy.
caption: Choose the stitch count from the perimeter. A round tube around an oblong case leaves space at the sides, which is fine in soft fabric.

alt: Four steps. 1: wrap the yarn around two fingers so the tail crosses over the working yarn. 2: insert the hook under the ring, catch the working yarn, and pull up a loop, then ch 1; the ch 1 is not a stitch. 3: work the stated number of sc into the ring, over both strands of the ring and the tail. 4: pull the tail to close the center, then count the stitches.
caption: Round 1 starts in a magic ring. The ch 1 that closes the first loop is not a stitch.

alt: Base: rounds 1 to 5, drawn as rings from the center out. Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring, 6 stitches. Round 2: 2 sc in each st, 12 stitches. Round 3: (sc, 2 sc in next) 6 times, 18 stitches. Round 4: (sc 2, 2 sc in next) 6 times, 24 stitches. Round 5: (sc 7, 2 sc in next) 3 times, 27 stitches. Rounds 1 to 4 add 6 each. Round 5 adds 3, for the 27 the case needs.
caption: Step 1. Round 5 adds only 3 stitches, one in every eighth, to land on 27.

alt: The whole pouch by stitch count, as bars sized by stitch count. Round 1: 6, Round 2: 12, Round 3: 18, Round 4: 24, Round 5: 27, Rounds 6 to 18: 27. Base: rounds 1 to 5. Wall: 13 even rounds of 27, about 2.6 in tall at 5 rounds per inch.
caption: Step 2. Rounds 1 to 5 lie flat as the base. With no more increases, rounds 6 to 18 turn up into the wall.

alt: A flap of 6 rows worked over 9 of the 27 stitches on the last round, with a chain loop on the top row. Rows 1 to 5: 9 sc, ch 1 and turn. Row 6: sc 3, ch 4, skip 3, sc 3. The other 18 stitches stay open.
caption: Step 3. The flap is 9 of the 27 stitches. On row 6 the ch 4 replaces 3 skipped stitches and becomes the button loop.

alt: A pair of oatmeal crochet fingerless gloves
caption: Illustration. It draws a short thumb. This page makes a thumb opening only. Not a fitted pair.

alt: Worsted yarn and a hook for a pair of gloves
caption: Illustration. Worsted yarn and a hook. Not a weighed amount for a pair.

alt: Three steps. A flat ribbed cuff strip whose 9-stitch chain is the depth and whose rows go around. The strip sewn into a ring, with the seam marking where rounds join. The hand worked as a tube upward from the cuff, with a thumb gap on one side. A note says to pick up 4 stitches for every 5 row ends, so 30 rows become 24 stitches, and 28 by round 2.
caption: The cuff is sideways: its chain is the depth along the arm, and its rows go around the wrist. The hand's first round is made from the ends of those rows.

alt: A foundation chain of 9. The chain nearest the hook is skipped and the first sc goes into the 2nd chain from the hook, so row 1 has 8 sc.
caption: Step 1. Chain 9 for an 8-stitch cuff, about 2 inches deep. The cuff is worked sideways.

alt: Two steps. 1: the top of each stitch has a front loop, nearer you, and a back loop, farther away. For the rib, insert the hook under the back loop only. 2: the front loops left behind form a raised ridge on every row. The fabric stretches across the ridges, in the direction the rows stack up, so a band worked sideways stretches around the head.
caption: Back loop only from row 2 gives the cuff its stretch around the wrist.

alt: Round 2: 24 to 28, drawn as rings from the center out. Round 1: undefined, 24 stitches. Round 2: (sc 5, 2 sc in next) 4 times, 28 stitches.
caption: Step 2. Four increases take the hand from the wrist's 24 stitches to the knuckles' 28.

alt: Rounds shown unrolled as strips, with the join of each round marked. Correct: slip stitch into the top of the first sc, ch 1, and work the first sc of the next round into that same stitch; the joins stack in a straight line. Mistake: the first sc goes into the next stitch instead, so every join moves one stitch sideways and the seam slants.
caption: These rounds are joined. Starting each round in the same stitch as the join keeps the seam straight and the count at 28.

alt: Round 8 opened into a line of 28 stitch boxes: 11 single crochet, 5 skipped boxes under an arched chain of 5, then 12 single crochet. The gap is centered on stitch 14, opposite the join. The next round is 11 plus 5 plus 12, which is 28. A note shows that a chain of 6 over 4 skipped stitches gives 30.
caption: The chain replaces the skipped stitches one for one. That is why the next round still has 28.

alt: A pair of simple crochet slippers with a toe cap and a heel tab
caption: Illustration. A flat sole, a toe cap, and a heel. Not a worn pair.

alt: Worsted yarn, a hook, and a tape measure
caption: Illustration. Yarn and tools. The sole is still slippery.

alt: A toe cap sewn to one end of a rectangular sole
caption: Illustration. The marked end is the toe. The last row of the cap stays open.

alt: A short heel tab on the unmarked end of the sole
caption: Illustration. The heel is the unmarked end.

alt: Top view of a sole 14 stitches wide and 48 rows long. A toe cap 24 stitches wide and 16 rows deep is sewn to the first 16 rows of each side and gathered onto the 14 toe stitches. A heel wall 26 stitches long and 8 rows high wraps the heel end and 8 rows up each side. 24 rows of each side stay open. An inset shows a tape from one edge of the sole, over the foot, to the other edge: about 6 inches.
caption: The cap's width is the over-the-top measurement, not the sole width. Its extra stitches gather at the toe.

alt: Sole: 14 sc, 48 rows. Toe cap: 24 sc, 16 rows. Heel wall: 26 sc, 8 rows.
caption: The three pieces of one slipper, drawn to the same scale from the example counts.

alt: Two rows of single crochet. Correct: the turning ch 1 sits beside the edge and the first sc of the new row goes into the first stitch, the last one made on the row below, so the count stays the same. Mistake: the first sc goes into the ch 1, outside the edge, which adds a stitch and makes the edge flare.
caption: All three pieces are plain sc rows. Start each row in the edge stitch so the widths stay at 14, 24, and 26.

alt: A printed crochet pattern beside yarn and a hook on a desk
caption: Illustration. Read the materials and gauge notes before the first stitch line.

alt: Finger pointing at crochet pattern abbreviations on paper
caption: Illustration. One pattern line is a recipe — abbreviations, counts, and punctuation.

alt: Finger counting stitches on a cream swatch beside a printed pattern
caption: Illustration. Count after every row or round until the numbers stick.

alt: Diagram of four chain-top Vs numbered 1 through 4, and a loop still on the hook marked as not a stitch.
caption: Diagram. The number in parentheses is how many finished Vs you should have. The loop on the hook is not an extra stitch.

alt: Diagram of the repeat single crochet, then two single crochets in the next stitch, worked three times. It uses six old stitches and makes nine new stitches.
caption: Diagram. Count what the repeat uses, then what it makes, then multiply by how many times it says.

alt: Two pairs of hands mirroring each other, one crocheting left-handed and one right-handed
caption: Illustration. Same stitches, same fabric, opposite direction of travel.

alt: A left hand crocheting a cream swatch with an aluminum hook
caption: Illustration. Same stitches, opposite direction of travel.

alt: A left hand working a row of crochet from left to right across the fabric
caption: Illustration. The finished stitches of the row sit to the left of the hook, and the fabric still to be worked runs off to the right.

alt: A plain aluminum crochet hook held in the left hand, working a swatch of ivory yarn
caption: Illustration. An ordinary hook off the shelf. Both hands are working either way — the only thing that changes is which one holds the hook.

alt: Diagram comparing direction of travel. Right-handed rows go right to left and rounds counterclockwise. Left-handed rows go left to right and rounds clockwise.
caption: Diagram. The only change in the hands is the direction of travel.

alt: An orange ribbed crochet wallet with a jack-o'-lantern face, a green leaf tab, and a stem at the top
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet. In the pattern the stem stands on the back rim, behind the tab.

alt: The orange piece laid flat, with the ribs running vertically, before the face or the fold
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet.

alt: The closed orange wallet. The leaf tab folds over the front; sew the stem on the back rim, behind that tab
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet. The stem in the picture sits on the tab. The pattern puts it on the back rim.

alt: Diagram. The piece laid flat with vertical orange ribs. Stitch 1 at the top is the front rim, stitch 20 at the bottom is the back rim, and a dashed fold line runs between stitches 10 and 11. Rows run up and down from row 1 at the left to row 22 at the right.
caption: Diagram. Rows run up and down. The fold runs across the middle of every row.

alt: Diagram. A close-up of the top of a single crochet, with the hook in the back loop and the front loop left as a ridge. Three swatch options: back loop every row for 11 ribs over 22 rows, both loops for a flat face, or two shades of orange changing every 2 rows.
caption: Diagram. One raised rib for every two rows, on one face of the fabric.

alt: Diagram. A grid of the front half with rows 1 to 22 left to right and stitches 1 to 10 down from the rim. The leaf tab covers rows 10 to 13 on stitches 1 to 5. Triangle eyes span rows 5 to 7 and 16 to 18 on stitches 3 to 5. The nose covers rows 11 and 12 on stitches 6 and 7. A zigzag mouth runs from row 6 to row 17 on stitches 8 and 9.
caption: Diagram. Row k mirrors row 23 minus k. Stitch 1 is at the front rim.

alt: Diagram. Left, the flat piece with a 22 single crochet rim on each long edge and a fold line between stitches 10 and 11, with the two short sides marked as seams. Right, the folded pouch to scale, about 4.25 by 2.5 inches outside, with an ID-1 card inside and the inside about 3.9 by 2.4 inches on paper.
caption: Diagram. Fold right side out so the ribs and face stay outside.

alt: Diagram. The stem, a green strip 6 single crochet by 3 rows rolled into a small cylinder. The leaf tab, 3 stitches wide for 6 rows with a point on row 7. A side view of the tab sewn inside the back rim, rising over both rims and down the front, with a snap under the tip and the stem standing on the back rim.
caption: Diagram. The tab is the closure. The stem only decorates.

alt: A black crochet wallet with a pointed flap, a white web, a purple spider, and a loop over a button
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet. The pattern's web has five spokes.

alt: The black pointed flap before any embroidery
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet.

alt: The purple spider on the right side of the web, with the loop and button at the point
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet. The pattern uses five spokes.

alt: Diagram. A black rectangle 17 stitches wide. Rows 1 to 13 are the front, rows 14 to 26 the back, and rows 27 to 34 a pointed flap that decreases at both ends of each row, 15, 13, 11, 9, 7, 5, 3, then a three-together decrease. A chain-8 loop sits at the point.
caption: Diagram. The flap loses one stitch at each end of every row until it comes to a point.

alt: Diagram. The closed flap with five white spokes running from the point at row 34 to row 27 at stitches 2, 5, 8, 11, and 14, and three rings at rows 29, 31, and 33, each made of four segments that dip toward the point. A purple spider sits between the rings at rows 29 and 31 on the fourth spoke.
caption: Diagram. Spokes first, inner ring first, spider last.

alt: Diagram. Left, the abdomen: magic ring of 6, round 2 increases to 12, round 3 even, round 4 decreases to 6. The head: magic ring of 6 and one even round. Right, the head sewn to the abdomen with eight two-segment legs, four per side, bent at the knee.
caption: Diagram. Two tiny balls and eight stitched legs.

alt: Diagram. The loop at the point of the flap, chain 8 slip stitched to the same stitch. The closed wallet to scale, about 4.25 by 2.6 inches, with the flap about 1.6 inches below the fold, the loop 0.4 inch more, and the button near row 10 of the front at stitch 9. A dashed ID-1 card fits inside on paper.
caption: Diagram. Close the flap with cards inside before marking the button.

alt: A blocked crochet square pinned flat on a foam mat
caption: Illustration. Weave ends, then block — that order keeps the finish clean.

alt: Tapestry needle weaving a yarn end into crochet fabric
caption: Illustration. Weave through several stitches on the wrong side, then reverse direction once.

alt: A cream granny square pinned flat on a foam blocking mat
caption: Illustration. Pin to shape while damp — corners first, then mid-sides.

alt: Diagram comparing a tail woven straight through a row of stitches with a tail that runs out through several stitches and turns back on a different path.
caption: Diagram. The turn is what holds the end, not the distance.

alt: A single aluminum crochet hook beside one ball of ivory worsted-weight yarn
caption: Illustration. This is genuinely the whole shopping list.

alt: Beginner crochet kit flat lay with hook yarn needle and markers
caption: Illustration. This is genuinely the short shopping list.

alt: Two crochet hook heads side by side, one with a pointed tapered tip and one with a flat inline head
caption: Illustration. Tapered on the left, inline on the right. Most people develop a firm preference within a week.

alt: Four balls of yarn in a row: smooth pale solid, very dark, variegated, and fuzzy
caption: Illustration. Only the first one shows you where to put the hook.

alt: A hook gauge plate, a blunt tapestry needle, split-ring stitch markers and a tape measure
caption: Illustration. The hook gauge is the one accessory worth buying early.

alt: Diagram. More stitches than the pattern in four inches means try a larger hook. Fewer stitches means try a smaller hook. Measure again after the change.
caption: Diagram. Change one hook size, then measure the middle of a new swatch. The first swatch does not become the right size by stretching it.

alt: Three steps. A yarn label reading 200 yards per 100 grams gives 2 yards per gram. One finished piece weighs 14 grams on a kitchen scale. 14 times 2 is 28 yards, plus 10 to 20 percent. The numbers are examples.
caption: Yards per gram from the label, grams from the scale. The example numbers are invented.

alt: Laptop and tablet beside yarn and a crochet hook on a desk
caption: Illustration. Start with trusted libraries — then check the pattern still opens.

alt: Laptop open beside a printed crochet pattern yarn and hook
caption: Illustration. Start with known libraries, then verify the pattern page still opens.

alt: Notebook project list beside yarn and a hook
caption: Illustration. Clear materials, gauge, and photos beat a pretty cover shot alone.

alt: A purple crochet wallet with a small black witch hat, an orange band, and a button under the brim
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet.

alt: The purple rectangle before it is folded, with the buttonhole worked into the row
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet. In the pattern the hole is centered.

alt: The small black hat with an orange band, beside a ball of purple yarn
caption: Illustration, not a photograph of a made wallet.

alt: Diagram. A rectangle 17 stitches wide, one grid square per stitch. Rows 1 to 12 are the front, rows 13 to 24 the back, rows 25 to 33 the flap. Row 31 has a buttonhole of 3 chains over 3 skipped stitches. Row 33 decreases at both ends to 15. Dashed lines mark the folds at rows 12 and 24.
caption: Diagram. Three zones in one piece. The chain edge becomes the front rim.

alt: Diagram. Row 31 is 7 single crochet, chain 3, skip 3, 7 single crochet. Row 32 is 7, then 3 into the chain space, then 7, back to 17. The closed wallet to scale, about 4.25 by 2.4 inches, with the button near row 7 of the front at stitch 9, about 1.3 inches below the top fold.
caption: Diagram. Count 17 after row 32. The hole sits over stitches 8 to 10.

alt: Diagram. The cone in 5 rows: row 1 in orange, 5 stitches, then black, 5, 3, 3, and 1. A separate black brim strip of 8 stitches. On the closed flap, the brim lies on row 30 centered on stitch 9, the tip reaches row 25 at the top fold, and the buttonhole on row 31 sits just below the brim.
caption: Diagram. Hat band in orange, the rest in black. Keep row 31 clear.

alt: Diagram. A side view with the front folded up against the back and the divider between them, its lower edge at the fold and its top one row below the rim, making two pockets. A side seam of single crochet passes through front, divider, and back, one per row end, 12 per side.
caption: Diagram. Two pockets of the same width, sealed by the same side seams.

alt: Basket of red green and cream Christmas crochet yarns
caption: Illustration. Match yarn to the job — ornaments, gnomes, and trees ask for different things.

alt: Smooth worsted yarn beside sparkly Christmas yarn
caption: Illustration. Sparkle photographs well and fights you on small stitches.

alt: Matte red and green Christmas yarn beside a sparkly metallic skein
caption: Illustration. Matte worsted is easier for small stitches than glitter yarn.

caption: Yards per gram from the label, grams from the scale. The example numbers are invented.

alt: Yarn balls from thin lace weight to bulky lined up by size
caption: Illustration. Weight categories tell you thickness — not brand quality.

alt: Thin fingering yarn strand beside worsted yarn for comparison
caption: Illustration. Thinner yarns need more stitches and usually a smaller hook.

alt: Four cream yarn cakes lined up from thin to bulky
caption: Illustration. Match thickness first — then check yardage and fiber.
